correctness.rationale: In every characteristic other than two the commutator is twice the wedge of odd parts; both even parts supply 2^n unconstrained coordinates. A nonzero first linear part forces a unique scalar relationship on v_1. The degree-four kernel is u_1∧Λ²W, and at n=6 the degree-six equation is surjective in v_5, giving an affine bundle of odd dimension 48 at n=6. A pair with only v_1 nonzero belongs to its closure by the shear (u+t v,v). For n≤5 the remaining both-zero locus also lies in the closure: wedging v_3 by a linear vector has kernel by dimension for n≤4 and by the singularity of the alternating 5×5 map for n=5. At n=6 the both-zero locus is the middle alternating-pairing hypersurface, of polar rank 40, with 12 additional odd coordinates. It is rational and irreducible of odd dimension 51, hence cannot lie in the first closure; the converse is excluded by the nonzero linear part. Adding the even factor gives dimensions 112 and 115. Independent replay used ordered rank-one linear pairs, basis monomial maps, and complementary triples to recover both symbolic point counts. The repaired proof and its finite-field comparison have the same equations, hypotheses and conclusions and were checked against these arguments.
residual_risks: The verification concerns the reduced pair variety, not the defining scheme or characteristic two; the symbolic count replay is not the proof of irreducibility.
